analyst_view.overall: Club Brugge (9th) and Liverpool (8th) are level on 9 points, so the winner moves close to the top eight. Brugge have won their last three in Europe and won 5-1 at Mechelen on Saturday, with Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line, but Joel Ordóñez (metatarsal fracture, already in the numbers) and winger Jan Virgili (groin, not in the numbers) are out according to the latest Liverpool-side previews. Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday; Cody Gakpo (calf, picked up with the Netherlands) has not trained since and is out, Ryan Gravenberch (heel) is 'day to day' under Andoni Iraola and may need a late test, and Ekitiké (counted), Leoni and Bradley are not expected to feature, while Van Dijk and Frimpong are available. Spanish referee Alejandro Hernández Hernández (4.9 cards a game) is named and the numbers already add about 28% to cards for him. Since the last view the only change is a slightly bigger goals cut, adding Virgili's absence to Gakpo's.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, 1.8 of them Liverpool's, already up a little for both attacks' form and down for Ekitiké and Ordóñez. Gakpo, one of Liverpool's regular scorers, is out with a calf injury and Brugge winger Jan Virgili is out with a groin problem; the numbers list neither, so I take about 4% off, to about 3.26. Isak and Wirtz are fit for Liverpool and Tresoldi is in form for Brugge, which keeps the cut small.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.3 corners, 6 of them Liverpool's, and already add about 5% for Liverpool's high corner count lately. Liverpool's width with Frimpong back and Brugge sitting compact at home fit that picture even without Gakpo and Virgili, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4 cards and already add about 28% for referee Hernández Hernández, who averages 4.9 a game, plus 5% for Brugge's busy recent card count. There is no rivalry and nothing in the team news changes the temperature of the game, so I stay at 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.8 shots and have already pushed both sides up by 15-19% for their recent shooting. Gakpo's and Virgili's absences change who shoots more than how often, and Liverpool's 22 shots in the numbers rest on Isak, Wirtz and Szoboszlai, who are fit, so I stay at about 35.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 shots on target, already up about 9% for both sides' recent accuracy. Tresoldi is sharp for Brugge and Liverpool still have Isak and Wirtz, so beyond the small goals cut for the two missing wide forwards I stay at about 11.8.
